role.title: Senior Product Designer, AI experiences
role.team: A product squad designing flows where a model suggests, drafts or acts for the user

outcomes.text: Users can tell what the model did, correct it and undo it
outcomes.measure: share of model actions users accept, edit or undo, read beside support contacts about the feature

outcomes.text: Design quality of model output is checked by evals, not by eye
outcomes.measure: design-owned eval cases in the release suite, and releases that met them

outcomes.text: The experience stays usable when the model is slow, wrong or unavailable
outcomes.measure: flows with a designed failure and fallback state, out of all model-backed flows

competencies.name: Interaction design for uncertainty
competencies.description: Designs for a model that is sometimes wrong: confidence, review, correction and undo.

anchors.2: Adds an error message but no way to correct or undo.
anchors.3: Designs review, correction and undo, and a state for low confidence.
anchors.4: Does all of 3 and decides where the user must confirm before the model acts, and why.

competencies.name: Eval design
competencies.description: Turns design quality into eval cases with pass rules.

anchors.1: Relies on trying a few prompts by hand; no written cases.
anchors.2: Writes happy-path cases only, or cases with no pass rule.
anchors.3: Writes cases for the main failure modes, each with a pass rule, and sets a pass line for release.
anchors.4: Does all of 3, adds cases from real failure reports, and says how the suite stays honest as the model changes.

competencies.name: Cost judgment
competencies.description: Knows that design choices (streaming, retries, regenerate buttons) change cost per task.

anchors.2: Mentions cost but cannot estimate it per task.
anchors.3: Estimates cost per task as tokens per task and price per token, and compares it with the value of the task.
anchors.4: Does all of 3 and names the cheaper path (smaller model, caching, no model) and the quality it would trade.

competencies.name: Restraint: knowing when not to use a model
competencies.description: Chooses a template, a default or a plain form where a model adds risk or cost.

anchors.1: Uses a model for every step, including arithmetic and irreversible actions.
anchors.2: Accepts a non-model option only when prompted.
anchors.3: Unprompted, keeps at least one step out of the model and says why (accuracy, cost or liability).
anchors.4: Does all of 3 and sets the rule for when the step could move to a model later, with the evidence that would justify it.

competencies.name: Research and evidence
competencies.description: Tests designs with users and changes them on what users do.

anchors.2: Tests late, or only for usability defects.
anchors.3: Tests early with users and names what each round changed.
anchors.4: Does all of 3 and can show a design the evidence overturned.

stages.name: Work sample
stages.task: You get a flow where a model drafts a message the user sends to their own customer, with 30 anonymised drafts and what users changed. In 90 minutes, redesign the review step: show the states (draft, low confidence, error, model unavailable), the eval cases that would check the drafts, what each regenerate or retry costs, and which parts should be a template instead of a model. AI tools are allowed and expected; say where you used them.

anchors.4: Does all of 3, adds cases from real failure reports, and says how the suite stays honest as the model changes.

questions.text: Show me a design where the system could be wrong. How did the user find out and recover?
Tell me about research that changed your design.
follow_ups: What did you expect to find?

questions.text: How do you decide when a user must confirm before the system acts?
follow_ups: Give an example where you got it wrong.

stages.name: Structured interview: judgment in AI use

questions.text: How would you turn 'the drafts feel off' into something an eval can check?
A regenerate button doubles the cost of the feature. What do you do?
Tell me about a time you replaced a model-driven element with something simpler.
How do you test a design whose output changes every time?

steps: Each interviewer records every score, with written evidence, before the debrief starts. Scores recorded after it starts do not count.
Interviewers do not see each other's scores or discuss the candidate until the debrief starts.
The facilitator runs run.py score and shares the packet. Nobody states a view first.
For each flagged competency, the interviewers read their evidence aloud, lowest score first, and compare it with the anchors.
Scores do not change in the debrief. If an interviewer finds they misread an anchor, the decision note says so.
The hiring manager decides against the band and the evidence, and writes the decision note; check-note checks it before it is sent.
